messages.content: What is the largest planet in the universe?

function.name: space_star_info
function.description: Retrieve information about a particular star in the universe. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

information.description: The type of information needed about the star.

message.content:
The largest planet that has been confirmed in our own Solar System is **Jupiter** – it has a mass about 318 times that of Earth and a diameter roughly 11 times Earth's.

In terms of exoplanets (planets orbiting other stars), the record holder for size is still a bit uncertain because many of the candidates are “hot Jupiters” whose radii can be inflated by intense stellar radiation. As of the most recent surveys, the largest planet with a reliable measurement is **HD 100546 b**, which has a radius about **6.9 ± 0.5 times that of Jupiter** (roughly 7–8 × 10⁴ km across). Other very large exoplanets include:

| Planet | Approximate Radius | Notes |
|--------|--------------------|-------|
| HD 100546 b | ~6.9 R_J | Young, gas‑giant, still forming |
| WASP‑17b | ~1.99 R_J | Extremely low density, bloated |
| HAT‑P‑32b | ~1.75 R_J | Hot Jupiter, inflated |

Because exoplanet discoveries are ongoing and some measurements rely on indirect methods (transit depth, radial velocity), the exact ranking can change as new data come in. However, HD 100546 b remains the best candidate for the largest planet currently known.

But we can provide known largest planets: Jupiter is largest in our solar system. Exoplanets: HD 100546 b (~6.9 times radius of Jupiter). Also WASP-17b (~1.99 Jupiter radii).
